answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so influence decays when paths encounter sparse cuts. A sybil cluster that lacks many honest cross-links has low conductance, trapping walk mass like a walnut drifting in an ocean rather than allowing it to wander freely. Cheeger-style bounds and min-cut transitivity therefore cap the cluster’s stationary reach and aggregate voting weight, even under coordinated attestations.
